endpoints.summary: Show the identity behind the current credential
endpoints.description: Returns the identity of the authenticated user: user id, email, name, role, buyer_id and staff flag. Useful to confirm which user and buyer the CLI is acting as.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, email, name, role, buyer_id, is_staff}.

endpoints.description: Creates an approval step for the buyer. IMPORTANT: when `action` is TIERS_APPROVAL the backend automatically seeds one default tier ("Nível Único Padrão") — you do not pass tiers here, and a tiers step without a tier would be invalid. A step is created NOT in use; putting it to work is done elsewhere. Both the uppercase value (RISK_SCORE) and the lowercase key (risk_score) are accepted on input, and the response always reads back the lowercase form. Requires the manager role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Name of the approval step.

params.name: condition
params.desc: What triggers the step. One of SETTING_CATEGORY, RISK_SCORE, SETTING_DOCUMENT, EXCEPTION_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted).

params.name: action
params.desc: What the step does. One of AUTOMATIC_APPROVAL, AUTOMATIC_REFUSAL, TIERS_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted). With condition EXCEPTION_APPROVAL only TIERS_APPROVAL is valid.

params.name: being_used
params.desc: Whether the step is already in use. Defaults to false (a draft).

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. 422 {errors} on validation (missing display_name/condition/action, or an action other than TIERS_APPROVAL when the condition is EXCEPTION_APPROVAL); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_step root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a rejection reason for the buyer. The name must be unique within the buyer. Requires the admin role or above (listing is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Name of the rejection reason (e.g. "Risco financeiro"). Must be unique among the buyer's reasons.

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, display_name}. 422 {errors} when the name is blank or already used by this buyer; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_steps_decision_reason root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Deletes one rejection reason by its id (see `settings approval-step decision-reason list`). IMPORTANT: the backend refuses to delete the buyer's LAST remaining reason — an approval step rejection would have nothing to pick — and answers 403 in that case, not 422. Check the list length before deleting. Requires the admin role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 echoing the deleted {id, display_name}. 403 {error} when it is the buyer's last remaining reason, when the reason belongs to another buyer, or when the policy denies access; 404 if the id is unknown; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the rejection reasons available to approval steps
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's rejection reasons (motivos de reprovação), ordered by display_name. These are the reasons an approver picks when refusing a supplier in an approval step. Returns the whole collection — this list is not paginated. There is no `show`: the list already carries every field. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.description: Renames one rejection reason by its id — get the id from `settings approval-step decision-reason list`. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New name of the rejection reason. Must be unique among the buyer's reasons.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, display_name}. 422 {errors} when the name is blank or already used; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the root is missing; 404 if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the reason belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's approval steps (etapas de aprovação), newest first. By default returns the steps NOT in use (drafts); pass --current_tab with any value to list the ones in use instead. Optional --search filters by display_name (partial match). Returns the whole collection — this list is not paginated. Requires the manager role or above.

params.name: current_tab
params.desc: Omit to list the steps not in use (being_used false); pass any value (e.g. 'being_used') to list the ones in use.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. `condition` and `action` come back as lowercase keys (e.g. risk_score, automatic_approval) even when created with the uppercase form. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.description: Shows one approval step by its id — get the id from `settings approval-step list`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer, so a foreign id never resolves); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates one approval step by its id (see `settings approval-step list`). Only the fields you pass change. Same enum rules as `create`. Requires the manager role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New name of the approval step.

params.name: condition
params.desc: What triggers the step. One of SETTING_CATEGORY, RISK_SCORE, SETTING_DOCUMENT, EXCEPTION_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted).

params.name: action
params.desc: What the step does. One of AUTOMATIC_APPROVAL, AUTOMATIC_REFUSAL, TIERS_APPROVAL (the lowercase key is also accepted).

params.name: being_used
params.desc: Whether the step is in use.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, display_name, condition, action, being_used}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. a blank display_name); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_approval_step root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the buyer's bank information documents
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's bank information documents (dados bancários — SettingBankInformation), ordered by display order then display_name. A buyer has at most one enabled bank information document. By default returns the enabled documents; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. Each item carries the applicability flags national_pj/national_pf/international, which tell for which category legal_entity (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the document is available. This is a source of the `setting_document_id` a future `settings category risk create` will need: pick a document whose applicability flag matches the category's legal_entity (national_pj for a PJ category, national_pf for PF, international for INTERNATIONAL).

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled documents, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id}. The three boolean flags mark the category legal_entities (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the document applies to. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show the bank information document with its editable settings
endpoints.description: Shows one bank information document (dados bancários) of the buyer by its id — get the id from `settings bank-information list`. On top of the list fields it returns everything `settings bank-information update` can change, plus the nested `setting_document_review` (`review_type` and `expires_on_in_days`). Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, renew_at_in_days, allow_pf_bank_account, block_supplier_on_expiry, send_document_reviewed_event, webhook_reference, setting_document_review:{id, review_type, expires_on_in_days}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates one bank information document by its id (see `settings bank-information list`). Only the fields you pass change. There is no create/destroy for this document — the buyer has it from the start, you only configure it. Requires the admin role or above (reading is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Label shown to the supplier.

params.name: renew_at_in_days
params.desc: Days after approval when the document must be renewed (0 = never).

params.name: allow_pf_bank_account
params.desc: Whether a supplier may inform a personal (PF) bank account.

params.name: setting_grouper_id
params.desc: Id of the review group that reviews this document — from `settings setting-grouper list`. Must belong to the same buyer.

params.name: block_supplier_on_expiry
params.desc: Whether the supplier is blocked when this document expires.

params.name: send_document_reviewed_event
params.desc: Whether a webhook event is emitted when this document is reviewed.

params.name: webhook_reference
params.desc: Free-text reference sent along with the webhook event.

params.name: setting_document_review_attributes
params.desc: JSON object with the nested review settings. Requires the review's own `id` (from `settings bank-information show`) plus the field to change, e.g. '{"id":"<review-id>","expires_on_in_days":90}'. `expires_on_in_days` must be one of 0, 30, 90, 180, 360, 720, 1080.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated document in the same shape as `settings bank-information show`. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. an expires_on_in_days outside the allowed set); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_bank_information root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a new document field for the buyer. field_type must be one of: currency, select, text_input, upload, multi_select. When field_type is select or multi_select, options must contain at least 2 entries. level must be one of: supplier, qualification (default supplier). display_name is required; name is auto-generated from display_name when omitted.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Human-readable label of the field (required, unique per buyer among enabled fields).

params.name: name
params.desc: Internal identifier (unique per buyer). Auto-generated from display_name when omitted.

params.name: hint
params.desc: Optional helper text shown alongside the field.

params.name: field_type
params.desc: Field type. One of: currency, select, text_input, upload, multi_select. select and multi_select require options with at least 2 entries.

params.name: level
params.desc: Scope of the field. One of: supplier, qualification. Defaults to supplier.

params.name: national_pf
params.desc: Available for national individual (PF) suppliers. Defaults to true.

params.name: national_pj
params.desc: Available for national company (PJ) suppliers. Defaults to true.

params.name: international
params.desc: Available for international suppliers. Defaults to true.

params.name: availability_on_request
params.desc: Visibility in supplier requests. One of: hidden, optional, required. Defaults to hidden.

params.name: availability_on_qualification
params.desc: Visibility during qualification. One of: hidden, optional, required. Defaults to hidden.

params.name: options
params.desc: Array of string options. Required (at least 2) when field_type is select or multi_select.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. missing display_name, or select/multi_select without at least 2 options); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_buyer_document body root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Disables an enabled buyer document field for the buyer, archiving the setting. When `disable_buyer_documents` is true, the associated buyer documents are archived as well. The `id` identifies the enabled SettingBuyerDocument to disable — resolve it from `settings buyer-document list` (pending, plan P1).

params.name: disable_buyer_documents
params.desc: When true, also archives the buyer documents associated with the field

endpoints.response: 200 with the disabled document {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if no enabled document matches the id; 400 Rails default {status, error} when disable_buyer_documents is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below admin); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Enables a previously disabled buyer document field for the buyer, unarchiving the setting and its associated buyer documents. The `id` identifies the disabled SettingBuyerDocument to enable — resolve it from `settings buyer-document list` (pending, plan P1; use the disabled/archived listing).

params.name: id
params.desc: The id of the disabled SettingBuyerDocument to enable (from `settings buyer-document list`)

endpoints.response: 200 with the enabled document {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if no disabled document matches the id; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below admin); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's supplier/qualification document fields (SettingBuyerDocument), ordered by their display order. By default returns the enabled fields; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. This command is the source of the <id> consumed by `settings buyer-document show` and `settings buyer-document update`.

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled fields, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.description: Sets the display order of the buyer's enabled document fields. `identifiers` is a comma-separated list of SettingBuyerDocument ids in the desired final order; ids not belonging to the buyer are ignored. Resolve the ids from `settings buyer-document list` (pending, plan P1) and pass them in the order you want.

params.name: identifiers
params.desc: Comma-separated SettingBuyerDocument ids in the desired final order (e.g. "id1,id2,id3")

endpoints.response: 200 with the reordered enabled documents as an array of {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below admin); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Shows a single document field by its id (get the id from `settings buyer-document list`). Scoped to the current buyer — an id from another buyer returns 404.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access.

endpoints.description: Updates an existing (enabled) document field by its id (get the id from `settings buyer-document list`). Disabled fields cannot be updated (404). Scoped to the current buyer — an id from another buyer returns 404. When field_type is select or multi_select, options must contain at least 2 entries.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Human-readable label of the field (unique per buyer among enabled fields).

params.name: name
params.desc: Internal identifier (unique per buyer).

params.name: hint
params.desc: Optional helper text shown alongside the field.

params.name: field_type
params.desc: Field type. One of: currency, select, text_input, upload, multi_select. select and multi_select require options with at least 2 entries.

params.name: level
params.desc: Scope of the field. One of: supplier, qualification.

params.name: national_pf
params.desc: Available for national individual (PF) suppliers.

params.name: national_pj
params.desc: Available for national company (PJ) suppliers.

params.name: international
params.desc: Available for international suppliers.

params.name: availability_on_request
params.desc: Visibility in supplier requests. One of: hidden, optional, required.

params.name: availability_on_qualification
params.desc: Visibility during qualification. One of: hidden, optional, required.

params.name: options
params.desc: Array of string options. Required (at least 2) when field_type is select or multi_select.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, display_name, field_type, level, disabled, order}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. select/multi_select without at least 2 options); 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown, disabled, or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a supplier category for the buyer. Only the category's own settings are set here — risks (documents) are attached by a separate command. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Display name of the category (must be unique among the buyer's enabled categories)

params.name: legal_entity
params.desc: Legal entity the category applies to. Defaults to PJ when omitted.

params.name: renew_at_in_days_after_approval
params.desc: Days after approval to schedule the qualification renewal (0 = never renew). Defaults to 0.

params.name: force_processing_on_renewal
params.desc: On re-qualification, force expired renewable documents into a new blocking processing version. Defaults to false.

params.name: monitor_on_qualification_start
params.desc: Enable supplier monitoring at the start of qualification. Defaults to false.

params.name: monitor_after_approval
params.desc: Enable supplier monitoring after the qualification is approved. Defaults to false.

params.name: monitor_after_refusal
params.desc: Enable supplier monitoring after the qualification is refused. Defaults to false.

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, display_name, legal_entity, disabled, renew_at_in_days_after_approval, force_processing_on_renewal, monitor_on_qualification_start, monitor_after_approval, monitor_after_refusal, setting_risks} (setting_risks is [] on a fresh create). 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. blank or duplicate display_name, or a legal_entity outside PJ/PF/INTERNATIONAL); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_category root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Disables a category by its id (see `settings category list`). Unlike `settings category enable`, the id is a positional argument (path param), not a flag. Requires the admin role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with the affected category in the same shape as `settings category show` (disabled is now true). 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the category belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a copy of an existing category (including its risks), naming it with a "(cópia)" suffix. The source category is identified by the `--setting-category-id` flag (a top-level query param, NOT a positional argument), whose value comes from `settings category list`. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: setting_category_id
params.desc: Id of the category to duplicate; comes from `settings category list`.

endpoints.response: 200 with the newly created duplicate in the same shape as `settings category show`. 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_category_id is missing or unknown; 422 {errors} when the duplication fails; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Enables a previously disabled category so it can be used again. The category is identified by the `--setting-category-id` flag (a top-level query param, NOT a positional argument), whose value comes from `settings category list`. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: setting_category_id
params.desc: Id of the category to enable; comes from `settings category list`.

endpoints.response: 200 with the affected category in the same shape as `settings category show` (disabled is now false). 404 Rails default {status, error} when setting_category_id is missing or unknown; 403 {error} when the category belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's supplier categories (both enabled and disabled). Each category carries the `id` used as `category_id` when creating a supplier (see `supplier create`). v1 returns every category unfiltered — filter over the JSON on the client side. Future query filters: tab (disabled), search[display_name], search[legal_entity], page.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, legal_entity, disabled}. `legal_entity` is one of PJ, PF, INTERNATIONAL. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires the manager role or above).

endpoints.summary: Attach a document to a category as a risk
endpoints.description: Attaches a SettingDocument to a category with a risk score (creates a risk). `category_id` comes from `settings category list`. `setting_document_id` is the id of a SettingDocument (a supplier field / check / certificate / bank information) — obtain it from the document-list commands (`settings supplier-field list`, `settings check list`, `settings certificate list`, `settings bank-information list`), which list every enabled document with its applicability flags; `settings category risk list` only lists documents already attached to a category. IMPORTANT: the API does NOT filter by legal entity. The web screen only offers documents whose applicability matches the category's `legal_entity` (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL), but this endpoint accepts ANY existing document regardless of that match — attach only documents compatible with the category's legal entity. Attaching a `setting_document_id` already present in the category is idempotent: it updates that risk's score instead of creating a second one (200).

params.name: setting_document_id
params.desc: UUID of the SettingDocument to attach. Get it from the document-list commands — `settings supplier-field list`, `settings check list`, `settings certificate list`, `settings bank-information list` — which list every enabled document with its applicability flags (national_pj / national_pf / international); pick a document whose applicability matches the category's legal_entity (the API does NOT enforce it). `settings category risk list` only returns documents ALREADY attached to a category, so it is not the source for a new attachment (re-attaching an already-present document just updates its score).

params.name: risk
params.desc: Risk score for the document. One of 0 (Sem risco), 7 (Risco muito baixo), 20 (Risco baixo), 60 (Risco alto), 100 (Risco muito alto).

params.name: trigger_sync
params.desc: When true, enqueues a background job that propagates the new document to existing suppliers of the category. Optional; defaults to false.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, setting_document_id, risk, setting_document:{id, display_name, type}}. 422 {errors} when the setting_document_id does not exist; 400 (bad request) when the setting_risk root is absent; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the category is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Detach a document from a category (archive the risk)
endpoints.description: Detaches a document from a category by the risk `id` (from `settings category risk list`). The risk is marked for archival and a background job removes the attached document from the category's suppliers; the risk row is returned immediately.
endpoints.response: 200 with the archived {id, setting_document_id, risk, setting_document:{id, display_name, type}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the risk belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the risks (attached documents) of a category
endpoints.description: Lists the documents attached to one category as risks. A risk links a SettingDocument to the category with a risk score. `category_id` comes from `settings category list`. Each entry carries the `id` (the risk id) consumed by `settings category risk update|delete`, the `setting_document_id`, the `risk` score, and an embedded `setting_document` ({id, display_name, type}) to identify the document. The `type` is the SettingDocument subtype: Settings::SettingForm (supplier field), Settings::SettingCheck, Settings::SettingCertificate or Settings::SettingBankInformation. Scoped to the current buyer — a `category_id` from another buyer returns 404.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, setting_document_id, risk, setting_document:{id, display_name, type}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the category is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.description: Updates the risk score of an attached document by the risk `id` (from `settings category risk list`). Only the score changes; the document stays attached.

params.name: risk
params.desc: New risk score. One of 0 (Sem risco), 7 (Risco muito baixo), 20 (Risco baixo), 60 (Risco alto), 100 (Risco muito alto).

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, setting_document_id, risk, setting_document:{id, display_name, type}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the risk belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Show a supplier category with its risks
endpoints.description: Shows one supplier category by its id (see `settings category list` for available ids), including the full monitoring/renewal settings and its risks. Each embedded risk carries the `id` used as `risk_id` and the `setting_document_id` it points at. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, legal_entity, disabled, renew_at_in_days_after_approval, force_processing_on_renewal, monitor_on_qualification_start, monitor_after_approval, monitor_after_refusal, setting_risks:[{id, setting_document_id, risk}]}. `legal_entity` is one of PJ, PF, INTERNATIONAL. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the category belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates a supplier category by its id (see `settings category list`). Only the fields you pass are changed. Risks (documents) are managed by a separate command. Requires the admin role or above.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New display name of the category (must be unique among the buyer's enabled categories)

params.name: legal_entity
params.desc: Legal entity the category applies to.

params.name: renew_at_in_days_after_approval
params.desc: Days after approval to schedule the qualification renewal (0 = never renew).

params.name: force_processing_on_renewal
params.desc: On re-qualification, force expired renewable documents into a new blocking processing version.

params.name: monitor_on_qualification_start
params.desc: Enable supplier monitoring at the start of qualification.

params.name: monitor_after_approval
params.desc: Enable supplier monitoring after the qualification is approved.

params.name: monitor_after_refusal
params.desc: Enable supplier monitoring after the qualification is refused.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated category in the same shape as `settings category show`. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. blank or duplicate display_name, or an invalid legal_entity); 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the category belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's certificate documents (SettingCertificate), ordered by display order then display_name. By default returns the enabled certificates; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. Each item carries the applicability flags national_pj/national_pf/international, which tell for which category legal_entity (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the certificate is available. This is a source of the `setting_document_id` a future `settings category risk create` will need: pick a certificate whose applicability flag matches the category's legal_entity (national_pj for a PJ category, national_pf for PF, international for INTERNATIONAL).

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled certificates, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id}. The three boolean flags mark the category legal_entities (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the certificate applies to. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show the certificate with its editable settings
endpoints.description: Shows one certificate document (SettingCertificate) of the buyer by its id — get the id from `settings certificate list`. On top of the list fields it returns the internal `name` and `default_responsible_party`, plus the nested `setting_document_review` (`id`, `automatic_review_rule`). `name` is the certificate's internal identifier (e.g. CND_FEDERAL) and is different from `display_name`, which is the free, editable label shown to the supplier — INTERNAL_RESTRICTION_LISTS and CNAE_LISTS are the two certificates fed by CSV import; this command shows and updates them like any other certificate, it just does not expose the imported list items (restriction_lists/cnae_restrictions) themselves. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, name, default_responsible_party, setting_document_review:{id, automatic_review_rule}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates one certificate by its id (see `settings certificate list`). Only the fields you pass change. Requires the admin role or above (reading is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Label shown to the supplier.

params.name: default_responsible_party
params.desc: Who is responsible for providing this certificate.

params.name: setting_grouper_id
params.desc: Id of the review group that reviews this certificate — from `settings setting-grouper list`. Must belong to the same buyer.

params.name: setting_document_review_attributes
params.desc: JSON object with the nested review settings. Requires the review's own `id` (from `settings certificate show`) plus `automatic_review_rule`, e.g. '{"id":"<review-id>","automatic_review_rule":"only_refused"}'. `automatic_review_rule` must be one of disabled, only_refused, all_reviews.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated certificate in the same shape as `settings certificate show`. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. an automatic_review_rule outside the allowed set); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_certificate root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup), or when setting_grouper_id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's check documents (consultas — SettingCheck), ordered by display order then display_name. By default returns the enabled checks; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. Each item carries the applicability flags national_pj/national_pf/international, which tell for which category legal_entity (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the check is available. This is a source of the `setting_document_id` a future `settings category risk create` will need: pick a check whose applicability flag matches the category's legal_entity (national_pj for a PJ category, national_pf for PF, international for INTERNATIONAL).

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled checks, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id}. The three boolean flags mark the category legal_entities (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the check applies to. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show one check with its review settings
endpoints.description: Shows one check (consulta) of the buyer by its id — get the id from `settings check list`. On top of the list fields it embeds `setting_document_review`, which carries the review configuration: `review_type` (how the document is reviewed) and `automatic_review_rule` (whether reviewed documents are re-checked automatically). Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, setting_document_review:{id, review_type, automatic_review_rule, expires_on_in_days}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Update a check's review group or automatic review rule
endpoints.description: Updates one check by its id (see `settings check list`). Only two things are editable here: which review group reviews it (`setting_grouper_id`) and the nested review configuration (`setting_document_review_attributes`). Everything else about a check is fixed. Requires the admin role or above (reading is manager+).

params.name: setting_grouper_id
params.desc: Id of the review group that should review this check — from `settings setting-grouper list`. Must belong to the same buyer.

params.name: setting_document_review_attributes
params.desc: JSON object with the nested review settings. Requires the review's own `id` (from `settings check show`) plus the field to change, e.g. '{"id":"<review-id>","automatic_review_rule":"all_reviews"}'. `automatic_review_rule` is one of disabled, only_refused, all_reviews.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated check in the same shape as `settings check show`. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. an automatic_review_rule outside disabled/only_refused/all_reviews); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_check root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (scoped lookup); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a user for the current buyer and sends the invite e-mail. If a user with the same e-mail already exists on any buyer, the request fails (a buyer user cannot be re-created). Requires super_admin role.

params.name: name
params.desc: Full name of the user

params.name: email
params.desc: E-mail of the user (unique across buyer users; the invite is sent here)

params.name: role
params.desc: Permission role. One of the enum values (ascending privilege); defaults to member on the model but is required here.

endpoints.response: 200 with the created {id, name, email, role, discarded_at}. 422 {errors} on validation (blank name, invalid/blank e-mail, invalid role, or an e-mail that already belongs to a user); 400 {status, error} when the `user` body root is absent (params.expect runs before the policy check); 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires super_admin role); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Deactivates (soft-deletes / discards) a user of the current buyer by its id and removes its supplier links. The id is a positional argument (path segment), unlike `settings company-user enable`, which takes `--id`. Resolve the id with `settings company-user list`. A user cannot disable itself. Requires super_admin role.
endpoints.response: 200 with the deactivated {id, name, email, role, discarded_at} (discarded_at set). 404 {status, error} when the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the caller tries to disable itself or the policy denies access (requires super_admin role); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Reactivates (undiscards) a previously deactivated user of the current buyer. The id is read at the top level, so it is passed as `--id <uuid>` (a query param), NOT as a positional argument — this is the asymmetry with `settings company-user disable`, which takes the id positionally. Resolve the id with `settings company-user list`. Requires super_admin role.

params.name: id
params.desc: Id (uuid) of the user to reactivate; resolve it with `settings company-user list`.

endpoints.response: 200 with the reactivated {id, name, email, role, discarded_at} (discarded_at null). 400 {status, error} when the id query param is missing; 404 {status, error} when the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires super_admin role); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Cancels (deletes) a pending invite by its id (see `settings company-user invite list` for available ids) and returns the deleted invite. This only revokes an invite that has not been accepted yet; to deactivate an active user use the company-user commands instead.
endpoints.response: 200 with the deleted {id, email, role, created_at}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the invite belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Sends an e-mail invite to join the buyer as a new user and returns the created pending invite. The person becomes an active user (in `settings company-user list`) only after they accept the invite; until then they stay in `settings company-user invite list`. Fails if the e-mail already has a pending invite or already belongs to an existing user.

params.name: email
params.desc: E-mail address of the person to invite (must not already have a pending invite or an existing user account)

params.name: role
params.desc: Role the invited user will receive (defaults to member when omitted)

endpoints.response: 201 with the created {id, email, role, created_at}. 422 {errors} on validation (blank/invalid e-mail, an e-mail already invited, or an e-mail that already belongs to an existing user); 400 when the buyer_invite body root is absent; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below super_admin); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the pending invites (buyer_invites) of the current buyer, ordered by created_at desc. A pending invite is NOT an active user: it is a person who was invited by e-mail but has not accepted yet. Once accepted, the invite is consumed and the person shows up in `settings company-user list` instead. Use the returned id with `settings company-user invite cancel`. Requires a super_admin (or above) credential.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, email, role, created_at}. The secret acceptance token is never exposed. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below super_admin).

endpoints.description: Lists the active users of the current buyer with id, name, email, role and soft-delete state, ordered by name. A user is active when discarded_at is null. Use it to resolve a user_id needed by other commands (e.g. adding a user to a review group). Requires an admin (or above) credential.
endpoints.response: 200 with array of {id, name, email, role, discarded_at}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (caller below admin).

endpoints.description: Updates ONLY the role of a buyer user by its id (see `settings company-user list` for available ids). name and email are ignored even if sent. Requires super_admin role.

params.name: role
params.desc: New permission role. One of the enum values (ascending privilege).

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated {id, name, email, role, discarded_at}. 422 {errors} on an invalid role; 404 {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the user belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access (requires super_admin role); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Move a document to another review group
endpoints.description: Moves a document (Settings::SettingDocument) of the buyer — certificate, bank information, form or check — to a different review group (SettingGrouper). The `id` identifies the document to move — resolve it from the matching type's list command (e.g. `settings certificate list`). The destination `setting_grouper_id` must belong to the same buyer — get it from `settings setting-grouper list`; a grouper from another buyer or an unknown id is rejected before any write.

params.name: setting_grouper_id
params.desc: Id of the destination review group — from `settings setting-grouper list`. Must belong to the same buyer as the document being moved.

endpoints.response: 200 with the moved document in the same shape as enable/disable, with the new setting_grouper_id. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. a document with the same internal name already enabled in the destination group); 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_document root is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer, or when setting_grouper_id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin role or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Disables an enabled document (Settings::SettingDocument) of the buyer — certificate, bank information, form or check. This has a wide side effect, not a cosmetic toggle: it also marks every setting_risk associated with the document for destruction and enqueues an archive job (Settings::Risks::ArchiveDocumentsJob) per affected risk, which will archive the suppliers' documents tied to those risks. The `id` identifies the enabled document to disable — resolve it from the matching type's list command (e.g. `settings certificate list`, `settings bank-information list`, `settings supplier-field list`).
endpoints.response: 200 with the disabled document {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, name, type}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, or is already disabled (the lookup only matches enabled documents); 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin role or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Enables a previously disabled document (Settings::SettingDocument) of the buyer — certificate, bank information, form or check. Unlike disable/change-grouper, the underlying route has no id in the path, so the target is passed as setting_document_id. Get the id from the disabled/archived listing of the matching type (e.g. `settings certificate list --tab disabled`, `settings bank-information list --tab disabled`, `settings supplier-field list --tab disabled`).

params.name: setting_document_id
params.desc: The id of the disabled document to enable (from the archived listing of its type — certificate, bank-information or supplier-field)

endpoints.response: 200 with the enabled document {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, name, type}. `type` is the raw Settings::SettingDocument STI value: Settings::SettingCertificate, Settings::SettingForm, Settings::SettingBankInformation or Settings::SettingCheck. 422 {errors} when enabling would break a model validation — most often another ENABLED document in the same review group already uses this document's name, since the uniqueness rule only applies to enabled documents; the document stays disabled. 400 Rails default {status, error} when setting_document_id is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, or is already enabled (the lookup only matches disabled documents); 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin role or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's customizable e-mail message templates with their current content. Each entry is identified by its template name. Possible templates: supplier_invite, qualification_approved, qualification_refused, document_review_pending.
endpoints.response: 200 with array of {template, content, updated_at}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access.

endpoints.description: Shows one e-mail message template by its template name (see `settings email-message list` for available names).
endpoints.response: 200 with {template, content, updated_at}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the template is unknown; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access.

endpoints.description: Updates the content of an e-mail message template for the buyer. Content is limited to 280 characters.

params.name: content
params.desc: New message content (max 280 characters)

endpoints.response: 200 with {template, content, updated_at}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. content over 280 chars); 400 Rails default {status, error} when content is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} if the template is unknown; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Show the current user's notification preferences
endpoints.description: Shows the notification preferences of the authenticated user: a master `enabled` switch plus per-event alert and pending-action flags. Run this before `settings notification update` to avoid overwriting flags blindly. Independent command (no reference chaining).
endpoints.response: 200 with {enabled, alert_rating, alert_invites, alert_reviews, alert_documents, alert_suppliers, alert_qualifications, alert_rule_added_suppliers, action_pending_user_grouper_review, alert_rule_added_suppliers_by_others, action_pending_user_approval_steps_review, action_pending_user_performance_evaluation_review} (all booleans). 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access.

endpoints.summary: Update the current user's notification preferences
endpoints.description: Updates the authenticated user's notification preferences. Only the flags you send are changed; omit a flag to leave it untouched. Run `settings notification show` first to read the current state and avoid blind overwrites.

params.name: enabled
params.desc: Master switch; when false, no notifications are sent regardless of the other flags

params.name: alert_rating
params.desc: Alert when a supplier rating changes

params.name: alert_invites
params.desc: Alert about supplier invitations

params.name: alert_reviews
params.desc: Alert about reviews

params.name: alert_documents
params.desc: Alert about documents

params.name: alert_suppliers
params.desc: Alert about suppliers

params.name: alert_qualifications
params.desc: Alert about qualifications

params.name: alert_rule_added_suppliers
params.desc: Alert when suppliers are added to a rule you own

params.name: action_pending_user_grouper_review
params.desc: Pending-action alert for grouper reviews assigned to you

params.name: alert_rule_added_suppliers_by_others
params.desc: Alert when suppliers are added to a rule by other users

params.name: action_pending_user_approval_steps_review
params.desc: Pending-action alert for approval-step reviews assigned to you

params.name: action_pending_user_performance_evaluation_review
params.desc: Pending-action alert for performance-evaluation reviews assigned to you

endpoints.response: 200 with the full notification object (same shape as `settings notification show`) echoing the new state. 422 {errors} on validation failure; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the user_notification body is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Set the weight of every ask of a pillar in one batch
endpoints.description: Sets the weight (1..100) of one or more asks (questions) of a performance pillar in a single call. pillar_id comes from `settings performance-pillar show` (or the pillars tree in `settings performance-evaluation show <evaluation_id>`). The keys of --weights are ask ids (see `settings performance-pillar show <pillar_id>` for the asks tree) — shape: {"<ask_id>": {"weight": 1..100}, ...}. An ask id that does not belong to this pillar returns 404. Blocked (403) while the buyer has an active performance cycle.

params.name: weights
params.desc: Weights by ask id: {"<ask_id>": {"weight": 1..100}, ...}. Every key must be an ask id belonging to the pillar.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, asks:[{id, weight}]} (the pillar with every ask's current weight, not just the ones just updated). 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. a weight outside 1..100); 404 Rails default {status, error} if pillar_id is unknown/belongs to another buyer, or if an ask id in --weights does not belong to this pillar; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above, or an active performance cycle blocks the edit); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Create an ask under a pillar
endpoints.description: Creates an ask (question) under a pillar. The pillar_id path argument comes from `settings performance-evaluation show <evaluation_id>` (pillars tree) or `settings performance-pillar show <pillar_id>`. display_name is required and must be unique within the pillar. criterion defaults to scale_1_to_5 when omitted. weight is not settable here — it starts at 1 and only changes via `settings performance-ask calibrate` (once exposed). Blocked (403) while the buyer has an active performance cycle.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Display name of the ask (unique per pillar).

params.name: description
params.desc: Free-text description of the ask.

params.name: criterion
params.desc: Answer criterion for this ask. Defaults to scale_1_to_5 when omitted.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, pillar_id, display_name, description, criterion, weight}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. missing/duplicated display_name or an invalid criterion); 404 Rails default {status, error} if pillar_id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above, or an active performance cycle blocks the edit); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Deletes an ask by its id (see `settings performance-pillar show <pillar_id>` for the asks of a pillar — there is no ask list/show). Blocked (403) while the buyer has an active performance cycle.
endpoints.response: 200 with the deleted {id, pillar_id, display_name, description, criterion, weight}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above, or an active performance cycle blocks the edit); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates an ask by its id (see `settings performance-pillar show <pillar_id>` for the asks of a pillar — there is no ask list/show). Rename via display_name, change description, and/or change criterion. Does not touch weight — use `settings performance-ask calibrate` (once exposed). Unlike create/destroy, update is NOT blocked by an active performance cycle.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New display name of the ask (unique per pillar).

params.name: description
params.desc: New free-text description of the ask.

params.name: criterion
params.desc: New answer criterion for this ask.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, pillar_id, display_name, description, criterion, weight}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. duplicated display_name or an invalid criterion); 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above — update is NOT gated by an active performance cycle, unlike create/destroy); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a performance evaluation for the buyer. It starts disabled (not yet in use) with no pillars — use `settings performance-evaluation enable` (once exposed) to move it to the enabled tab, and `settings performance-pillar create <evaluation_id>` (once exposed) to add pillars.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Display name of the evaluation (unique per buyer)

params.name: description
params.desc: Free-text description of the evaluation. Omit for an empty description (the model rejects null, not blank).

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, description, disabled, pillars:[]}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. missing or duplicated display_name); 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Disable a performance evaluation (move it to "Não utilizado")
endpoints.description: Disables a performance evaluation for the buyer, moving it from the enabled tab to the disabled/archived one. The evaluation and its pillars/asks are not deleted — it can be re-enabled later with `settings performance-evaluation enable`. The `<id>` identifies the evaluation to disable — resolve it from `settings performance-evaluation list`.
endpoints.response: 200 with the evaluation {id, display_name, description, disabled, pillars_count}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Enable a performance evaluation (move it to "Em uso")
endpoints.description: Enables a performance evaluation for the buyer, moving it from the disabled/archived tab to the enabled one. A performance evaluation is created disabled by default (see `settings performance-evaluation create`), so this is the command that puts a freshly created evaluation into use. The `id` identifies the evaluation to enable — resolve it from `settings performance-evaluation list --tab disabled` (or the default `list` if it is already enabled; enabling an already-enabled evaluation is a no-op success).

params.name: id
params.desc: The id of the SettingPerformanceEvaluation to enable (from `settings performance-evaluation list`)

endpoints.response: 200 with the evaluation {id, display_name, description, disabled, pillars_count}. 400 Rails default {status, error} when id is missing; 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's performance evaluations (Avaliação → Pilares → Perguntas hierarchy root). By default returns the enabled evaluations; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. Each item is a lean summary (pillars_count only) — use the returned id with `settings performance-evaluation show` to get the full tree of pillars and asks.

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled evaluations, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, description, disabled, pillars_count}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show one performance evaluation with its full tree
endpoints.description: Shows a single performance evaluation by its id (get the id from `settings performance-evaluation list`), embedding its full tree of pillars and, per pillar, its asks — this is the equivalent of the evaluation's web page in one call. Pillar and ask ids returned here are the ones consumed by `settings performance-pillar show|update|destroy` and `settings performance-ask update|destroy`.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, description, disabled, pillars:[{id, display_name, description, weight, require_comment_per_answer, require_evidence_per_answer, asks:[{id, display_name, description, criterion, weight}]}]}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates a performance evaluation by its id (see `settings performance-evaluation list`). Rename via display_name and/or change description. Does not touch disabled — use the enable/disable commands (once exposed) to move it between tabs.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New display name of the evaluation (unique per buyer)

params.name: description
params.desc: New free-text description of the evaluation.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, description, disabled, pillars:[...]}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. duplicated display_name); 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Set the weight of every pillar of an evaluation in one batch
endpoints.description: Sets the weight (1..100) of one or more pillars of a performance evaluation in a single call. evaluation_id comes from `settings performance-evaluation list` or `settings performance-evaluation show`. The keys of --weights are pillar ids (see `settings performance-evaluation show <evaluation_id>` for the pillars tree) — shape: {"<pillar_id>": {"weight": 1..100}, ...}. A pillar id that does not belong to this evaluation returns 404. Blocked (403) while the buyer has an active performance cycle.

params.name: weights
params.desc: Weights by pillar id: {"<pillar_id>": {"weight": 1..100}, ...}. Every key must be a pillar id belonging to the evaluation.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, pillars:[{id, weight}]} (the evaluation with every pillar's current weight, not just the ones just updated). 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. a weight outside 1..100); 404 Rails default {status, error} if evaluation_id is unknown/belongs to another buyer, or if a pillar id in --weights does not belong to this evaluation; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above, or an active performance cycle blocks the edit); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Create a pillar under an evaluation
endpoints.description: Creates a pillar under a performance evaluation. The evaluation_id path argument comes from `settings performance-evaluation list` or `settings performance-evaluation show`. display_name is required and must be unique within the evaluation. weight is not settable here — it starts at 1 and only changes via `settings performance-pillar calibrate` (once exposed). Blocked (403) while the buyer has an active performance cycle.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Display name of the pillar (unique per evaluation).

params.name: description
params.desc: Free-text description of the pillar.

params.name: require_comment_per_answer
params.desc: Whether a comment is required on every answer under this pillar. Defaults to false.

params.name: require_evidence_per_answer
params.desc: Whether evidence (attachment) is required on every answer under this pillar. Defaults to false.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, evaluation_id, display_name, description, weight, require_comment_per_answer, require_evidence_per_answer, asks:[]}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. missing or duplicated display_name); 404 Rails default {status, error} if performance_evaluation_id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above, or an active performance cycle blocks the edit); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Deletes a pillar by its id (see `settings performance-evaluation show <evaluation_id>` for the pillars tree). Also deletes all of its asks. Blocked (403) while the buyer has an active performance cycle.
endpoints.response: 200 with the deleted {id, evaluation_id, display_name, description, weight, require_comment_per_answer, require_evidence_per_answer, asks}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above, or an active performance cycle blocks the edit); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: Show one pillar with its asks
endpoints.description: Shows a single pillar by its id, embedding its asks ordered by creation — get the id from the pillars tree returned by `settings performance-evaluation show <evaluation_id>` (there is no pillar list/index). Ask ids returned here are the ones consumed by `settings performance-ask update|destroy` (once exposed).
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, evaluation_id, display_name, description, weight, require_comment_per_answer, require_evidence_per_answer, asks:[{id, display_name, description, criterion, weight}]}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates a pillar by its id (see `settings performance-evaluation show <evaluation_id>` for the pillars tree). Rename via display_name, change description, and/or toggle require_comment_per_answer / require_evidence_per_answer. Does not touch weight — use `settings performance-pillar calibrate` (once exposed). Unlike create/destroy, update is NOT blocked by an active performance cycle.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New display name of the pillar (unique per evaluation).

params.name: description
params.desc: New free-text description of the pillar.

params.name: require_comment_per_answer
params.desc: Whether a comment is required on every answer under this pillar.

params.name: require_evidence_per_answer
params.desc: Whether evidence (attachment) is required on every answer under this pillar.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, evaluation_id, display_name, description, weight, require_comment_per_answer, require_evidence_per_answer, asks:[...]}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. duplicated display_name); 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires admin or above — update is NOT gated by an active performance cycle, unlike create/destroy); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a review group for the buyer, optionally with members. Members are set via setting_grouper_users_attributes, whose user_id comes from `settings company-user list`.

params.name: display_name
params.desc: Display name of the review group (unique per buyer)

params.name: setting_grouper_users_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of member objects [{"user_id":"<uuid>"}]; user_id comes from `settings company-user list`. On update, pass {"id":"<join_id>","_destroy":true} to remove an existing member.

params.name: setting_documents_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of document association objects [{"id":"<setting_document_id>"}]. No CLI command exposes setting_document ids yet — this param is documented for completeness and optional.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, documents_count, users:[{id, user_id, name, email}]}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. blank or duplicate display_name, or when the display_name is missing); 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Deletes an empty review group by its id (see `settings setting-grouper list`). A group with attached documents cannot be deleted (403).

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's review groups (setting groupers) with their members. Each entry carries its members and the count of documents attached to the group. Use the returned id with `settings setting-grouper show|update|destroy`.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, documents_count, users:[{id, user_id, name, email}]}. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access.

endpoints.description: Shows one review group by its id (see `settings setting-grouper list` for available ids), including its members.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, documents_count, users:[{id, user_id, name, email}]}. 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the group belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates a review group by its id (see `settings setting-grouper list`). Rename via display_name; add members via setting_grouper_users_attributes (user_id from `settings company-user list`); remove a member by passing {"id":"<join_id>","_destroy":true}.

params.name: setting_documents_attributes
params.desc: JSON array of document association objects [{"id":"<setting_document_id>"}]. No CLI command exposes setting_document ids yet — documented for completeness and optional.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, documents_count, users:[{id, user_id, name, email}]}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. blank or duplicate display_name); 404 Rails default {status, error} if the id is unknown; 403 {error} when the group belongs to another buyer or the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the members of a review group
endpoints.description: Lists the users (members) of one review group (setting grouper). The setting_grouper_id path argument comes from `settings setting-grouper list`.
endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, user_id, name, email} — id is the membership (join) id, user_id/name/email identify the member. Empty array when the group has no members. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_grouper_id is unknown or belongs to another buyer (buyer-scoped); 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the buyer's supplier form documents
endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's supplier form documents (the 'Formulários' settings — SettingForm plus the bank-information document), ordered by display order then display_name. By default returns the enabled documents; pass --tab disabled to list the archived (disabled) ones instead. Each item carries the applicability flags national_pj/national_pf/international, which tell for which category legal_entity (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the document is available. This is a source of the `setting_document_id` a future `settings category risk create` will need: pick a document whose applicability flag matches the category's legal_entity (national_pj for a PJ category, national_pf for PF, international for INTERNATIONAL).

params.name: tab
params.desc: Which set to list: omit (or any value other than 'disabled') for enabled documents, or 'disabled' for archived ones.

endpoints.response: 200 with an array of {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id}. The three boolean flags mark the category legal_entities (PJ / PF / INTERNATIONAL) the document applies to. 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires manager or above).

endpoints.summary: Show one supplier field with its review settings
endpoints.description: Shows one supplier field (campo de fornecedor — SettingForm) by its id; get the id from `settings supplier-field list`. Returns everything `settings supplier-field update` can change plus the nested `setting_document_review`. Requires the manager role or above.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, display_name, disabled, national_pj, national_pf, international, setting_grouper_id, hint, renew_at_in_days, webhook_reference, default_responsible_party, block_supplier_on_expiry, send_document_reviewed_event, setting_document_review:{id, review_type, expires_on_in_days, automatic_review_rule}}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown OR belongs to another buyer (the lookup is scoped to the caller's buyer); 403 {error} when the policy denies access by role; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Updates one supplier field by its id (see `settings supplier-field list`). Only the fields you pass change. Same rule as create: a `setting_grouper_id` from another buyer answers 404 — a document cannot change hands. Requires the admin role or above (reading is manager+).

params.name: display_name
params.desc: New label of the field. Must stay unique among the buyer's enabled documents.

params.name: setting_grouper_id
params.desc: Move the field to another review group of YOUR buyer — from `settings setting-grouper list`. A group from another buyer returns 404.

params.name: hint
params.desc: Helper text shown to the supplier.

params.name: national_pj
params.desc: Whether the field applies to national companies (PJ).

params.name: national_pf
params.desc: Whether the field applies to national individuals (PF).

params.name: international
params.desc: Whether the field applies to international suppliers.

params.name: renew_at_in_days
params.desc: Days after approval when the field must be renewed (0 = never).

params.name: default_responsible_party
params.desc: Who fills the field: supplier or buyer.

params.name: block_supplier_on_expiry
params.desc: Whether the supplier is blocked when the field expires.

params.name: send_document_reviewed_event
params.desc: Whether a webhook event is emitted when the field is reviewed. Requires webhook_reference to be filled.

params.name: webhook_reference
params.desc: Free-text reference sent along with the webhook event.

params.name: disabled
params.desc: Archive (true) or restore (false) the field. Archiving records who did it.

params.name: setting_document_review_attributes
params.desc: JSON object with the nested review settings. Requires the review's own `id` (from `settings supplier-field show`), e.g. '{"id":"<review-id>","expires_on_in_days":90}'.

endpoints.response: 200 with the updated field in the same shape as `settings supplier-field show`. 422 {errors} on validation; 404 Rails default {status, error} when the id is unknown, belongs to another buyer, or the setting_grouper_id is from another buyer; 400 Rails default {status, error} when the setting_form root is missing; 403 {error} when the policy denies access; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.description: Creates a setting tag (marcador) for the buyer. Requires admin role or above.

endpoints.description: Deletes a setting tag by its id (see `settings tag list` for available ids). Requires admin role or above.

endpoints.description: Lists the buyer's setting tags (marcadores) as {id, display_name}, ordered by display_name. This is the source of the `setting_tag_ids` accepted by `supplier create`: resolve the id of each tag here before assigning tags to a supplier.

endpoints.description:
Registers a supplier under one category of the current buyer, starting its qualification (homologação). legal_entity must be one of: PJ (national company), PF (national individual), INTERNATIONAL. identifier is the CNPJ (PJ) or CPF (PF); masked or unmasked is accepted. category_id is required.

Reference chaining (resolve each id BEFORE calling this command):
  * --category-id ← `settings category list` (required).
  * --setting_tag_ids[] ← `settings tag list` (repeat the flag per tag).
  * --buyer-document-fields ← names from `settings buyer-document list`. Pass a JSON object mapping each document field name to its value, e.g. '{"cnpj_certificate":"12345"}'. When the chosen category has qualification-required document fields for the supplier's legal_entity, those field names must be present here or the create fails (422).

params.name: name
params.desc: Supplier name. When omitted for a PJ with a known CNPJ, it is filled from the CNPJ record (razão social).

params.name: legal_entity
params.desc: Legal entity type. One of: PJ (national company), PF (national individual), INTERNATIONAL.

params.name: country_code
params.desc: ISO country code of the supplier (e.g. BR).

params.name: identifier
params.desc: CNPJ (PJ) or CPF (PF) of the supplier; masked or unmasked is accepted. Ignored for INTERNATIONAL.

params.name: contact_email
params.desc: Contact email; when present, an invite is sent to this address.

params.name: category_id
params.desc: Category the supplier is registered under (id from `settings category list`).

params.name: setting_tag_ids
params.desc: Tag ids to apply to the supplier (id from `settings tag list`). Repeat the flag once per tag.

params.name: locale
params.desc: Locale used for the qualification/invite copy (defaults to pt-BR).

params.name: buyer_document_fields
params.desc: JSON object mapping document field names (from `settings buyer-document list`) to their values. Required when the category has qualification-required document fields for the supplier's legal_entity.

endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, identifier, legal_entity, state, tags:[{id, display_name}], supplier_category_id}. 422 {errors} on validation (e.g. invalid identifier/contact_email, or missing required qualification document fields); 404 Rails default {status, error} when category_id is unknown or belongs to another buyer; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (requires member or above); 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated.

endpoints.summary: List the buyer's suppliers (one page per call; total comes in headers)
endpoints.description: Lists the suppliers of the current buyer. Each entry is identified by its id (use it with `supplier show`). The response is PAGINATED: the body carries one page, and the page metadata comes back in headers (`total-count`, `total-pages`, `current-page`, `page-items`). `--format count` reports the buyer's TOTAL from that header, not the size of the page, so one call answers "how many suppliers does this buyer have". Use `--page N` to fetch a specific page; the CLI reports on stderr which page you are on and how many there are. No other filters in this version.
endpoints.response: 200 with one page of {id, name, identifier, legal_entity, state, tags:[{id, display_name}]}, plus the pagy headers (`total-count`, `total-pages`, `current-page`, `page-items`). A page past the last one returns an empty array (still 200). 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access.

endpoints.description: Shows one supplier of the current buyer by its id, taken from the :supplier_id path segment (get the id from `supplier list`). Returns the supplier panel.
endpoints.response: 200 with {id, name, identifier, legal_entity, state, tags:[{id, display_name}]}. 404 Rails default {status, error} when the supplier is unknown; 401 (empty body) when unauthenticated; 403 {error} when the policy denies access (e.g. the supplier belongs to another buyer).
